body.stem: Your team created a public IP named pip-web-01 and attached it to the IP configuration ipconfig-web-01 of network interface nic-web-01 in virtual network vnet-web. The site's DNS record resolves to the address of pip-web-01, and the web application answers requests from hosts inside vnet-web. Visitors on the internet report that the site does not load. The NSG nsg-web-01 is attached to nic-web-01. Which change should you make to restore the site for internet clients?

options.text: Add an inbound rule to nsg-web-01 that allows TCP 443 from the Internet tag
Add an outbound rule to nsg-web-01 that allows TCP 443 to the Internet tag
Change the public IP SKU from Standard to Basic so that inbound traffic is accepted without any rule
Change the public IP tier from Regional to Global so that inbound traffic from the Internet reaches nic-web-01

explanation.correct: A Standard SKU public IP address is closed to inbound traffic by default: traffic that arrives on it passes to the VM only when an NSG is attached and explicitly permits the intended inbound flow. Here the address is correctly associated with nic-web-01 and DNS resolves to it, and nsg-web-01 is attached to the NIC but contains no inbound rule, so every inbound connection on the web port is dropped before it reaches the VM. Adding an inbound rule to nsg-web-01 permitting TCP 443 from the Internet tag opens the intended path while leaving outbound traffic untouched.

perChoice.b: An outbound rule governs connections leaving the VM, not connections arriving at it. The site is unreachable for arriving clients, so permitting egress to the same port changes nothing for the reported symptom, and the existing outbound permission already covers outbound flows.
perChoice.c: Basic was retired on September 30, 2025, so it can no longer be used for new addresses, and the SKU is not freely editable after creation — the documented change is an upgrade from Basic to Standard, not a downgrade from Standard to Basic. Even where an old Basic address still exists, the remedy for blocked inbound traffic on a Standard address is an NSG rule.
perChoice.d: Global tier is a preview capability limited to Standard SKU and intended for front ends of a cross-region load balancer; it is not a switch that governs inbound traffic on a regional address attached to a NIC. Tier is also fixed at creation, so this change would not take effect.

body.stem: You support a regional Azure Load Balancer in East US 2 whose front-end IP configuration uses public IP address pip-lb-fe01. Today sessions through that front end stay on the Microsoft backbone, and the egress charges billed for the public IPv4 address are higher than the team expects. The team wants the supported resources behind this address to spend less time on the Microsoft network so that egress costs come down. Which change should you make?

options.text: Update pip-lb-fe01 in place so its routing preference becomes Internet, then attach it to the load balancer.
Create a new public IP address with the Internet routing preference, then attach it to the load balancer.
Create a new public IP address with the Global tier so traffic is anycast across regions, then attach it to the load balancer.
Create a new public IP address with the Standard v2 SKU so it is always zone-redundant, then attach it to the load balancer.

explanation.correct: The routing preference of a public IP address is fixed at creation time and cannot be edited afterwards, so the existing pip-lb-fe01 (Microsoft network) cannot be converted in place. Choosing the Internet routing preference is what moves traffic off the Microsoft backbone sooner and lowers egress charges for the supported resources that use the address, and it requires the Standard SKU. The way to apply it is therefore to create a second Standard public IP address with the Internet routing preference and point the load balancer's front-end IP configuration at that resource; once the front end is switched, the old address can be detached from the IP configuration and deleted.

perChoice.a: Routing preference is locked when the public IP address is created, so an in-place update of pip-lb-fe01 from Microsoft network to Internet is rejected. The address must be replaced rather than edited, so editing the current resource cannot deliver the requested behaviour.
perChoice.c: The Global tier provides anycast across regions and is intended for a cross-region Load Balancer. It is a preview feature limited to the Standard SKU, and it does not change how much of the path stays on the Microsoft network, so it does not reduce the egress charges the team is trying to cut.
perChoice.d: A Standard v2 address can be attached only to the Standard v2 NAT Gateway and to no other product or component, so it cannot serve the load balancer front end. Standard v2 also offers no routing preference at all, so it cannot deliver the requested behaviour in the first place.

body.stem: You have a public IP address pip-app-fe01 in resource group rg-app-prod of subscription sub-app-001. It is the public front end of the corporate load balancer pip-app-lb that serves the company portal. You need the address to end up in resource group rg-dr-prod of the same subscription, and later, after a corporate merger, in subscription sub-merger-002, with portal traffic flowing throughout the whole reorganization. Which sequence of actions should you use?

rows: Front-end IP configuration fe-ipconfig-app of public load balancer pip-app-lb (Standard)

options.text: Reassign it to rg-dr-prod while it stays attached to fe-ipconfig-app, then detach it from fe-ipconfig-app and move it to sub-merger-002.
Reassign it to rg-dr-prod while it stays attached to fe-ipconfig-app, then move it to sub-merger-002 while it stays attached to fe-ipconfig-app.
Detach it from fe-ipconfig-app before reassigning it to rg-dr-prod, then move it to sub-merger-002 while it stays detached.
Reassign it to rg-dr-prod while it stays attached to fe-ipconfig-app, then delete it and create a new public IP address in sub-merger-002 with the same static address and DNS name label.

explanation.correct: A Standard SKU public IP can be reassigned to another resource group inside the same subscription while it remains associated with its front-end IP configuration, so the load balancer keeps serving traffic with no interruption during the reorganization. Transferring the address into a different subscription is only supported while the address is detached, so it must first be unassociated from fe-ipconfig-app, then moved into sub-merger-002, where it can be reattached. Doing the resource-group change first while attached and the subscription change after detaching satisfies both requirements.

perChoice.b: A public IP address can cross into another subscription only while it is detached; the transfer is not supported while it remains attached to fe-ipconfig-app, so this plan would fail and would leave the front end without an address.
perChoice.c: Unassociating the address from fe-ipconfig-app ahead of the resource-group change takes the load balancer's public address offline, which contradicts the requirement that portal traffic keep flowing throughout the reorganization. The address can be moved between resource groups in the same subscription with the association left in place.
perChoice.d: Deleting the address releases it permanently and it cannot be recovered, so the portal's DNS record and any IP-based allow-lists would no longer match a live address, and Azure does not guarantee that a newly created address receives the same IP value or label. The address should be preserved by moving it rather than replacing it.

body.stem: You have a public IP address pip-app-fe-01 in resource group rg-app of subscription sub-001, deployed in East US 2. It is attached to the network interface nic-app-01 of virtual machine vm-app-01, and every application instance of that virtual machine runs in availability zone 2. The platform team wants the public address to be served from that single zone so that it matches where the application runs, and the DNS record that points to the address must keep resolving to the application afterwards. Which change should you make?

options.text: Create a new Standard public IP address with availability zone 2 selected, attach it to the network interface IP configuration, and update the DNS record.
Update the existing Standard public IP address in place: attach it to the network interface IP configuration and set its availability zone to 2.
Delete the existing public IP address, then create a new one with the same IP address value and availability zone 2 selected, attached to the network interface IP configuration.
Change the SKU of the existing Standard public IP address to Basic so that availability zone 2 can be set, then update the DNS record.

explanation.correct: The availability zone of a public IP address is fixed when the address is created and cannot be changed afterwards, so the zone-redundant address shown in the exhibit can never be moved into zone 2 by editing it. The workable path is to build a second Standard address with availability zone 2 selected, detach the old address from the IP configuration, associate the new one with the same IP configuration, and then update the DNS record so the name resolves to the new address value. A zonal address is tied to the health of that single zone, which matches the placement of the application's instances.

perChoice.b: An in-place update cannot move an existing address into a single availability zone, because zone selection is only available at creation time. Set-AzPublicIpAddress can adjust other properties of the resource, but the zone assignment stays as it was, so the address would remain served from all zones in the region.
perChoice.c: A static address is reserved for its public IP resource only until that resource is deleted, and once deleted the address value cannot be recovered or re-created. Deleting the address also detaches it from the IP configuration, so this route loses the current address value and still requires a DNS change.
perChoice.d: Basic SKU was retired on September 30, 2025, and Basic addresses offer no availability-zone choice at all, so downgrading to Basic is neither possible nor a way to select zone 2. SKU is chosen at creation and is not freely editable afterwards, and the only documented SKU move is the Basic-to-Standard upgrade path.

body.stem: You are standing up a new Azure Firewall named af-edge-v2 in the virtual network vnet-edge in East US 2, and it must have a public front end. The corporate edge firewall allow-lists that front end for inbound TCP 443, so the address value must never change while the firewall exists. The front end must keep accepting inbound connections from the internet even if a single availability zone in the region is lost, and a platform policy states that no new public IP address may be created with a SKU that Microsoft has already retired. Which configuration should you create for the front end?

rows: Public IP address resource to create
Front end of the older firewall af-edge-v1
af-pip-01: Basic SKU, Static assignment, IPv4, no availability zones

options.text: Create af-pip-02 with the Standard SKU, Static assignment and IPv4, deployed as zone-redundant in East US 2.
Create af-pip-02 with the Standard SKU, Static assignment and IPv6, deployed as zone-redundant in East US 2.
Create af-pip-02 with the Standard SKU, Dynamic assignment and IPv4, deployed as zone-redundant in East US 2.
Create af-pip-02 with the Basic SKU, Static assignment and IPv4, deployed as non-zonal in East US 2.

explanation.correct: Basic SKU public IP addresses were retired on September 30, 2025, so the new front end must use the Standard SKU, which is also the SKU that supports availability zones. Standard addresses are created with Static assignment, so the value is allocated up front and stays the same for as long as the public IP resource exists, which keeps the corporate edge allow-list valid. Standard is the only SKU that can be deployed as zone-redundant in East US 2, so the front end survives the loss of one zone. An Azure Firewall front-end IP configuration accepts a static IPv4 address, and IPv6 is not offered for that resource type, so the IPv4 static zone-redundant combination with the Standard SKU satisfies every stated requirement.

perChoice.b: An Azure Firewall front-end IP configuration does not accept IPv6 addresses; the supported combinations for that resource type are a static IPv4 address only, so an IPv6 address cannot be attached to af-edge-v2. The upstream allow-list is IPv4 as well, so this choice cannot satisfy the requirement even though its SKU, assignment and zone handling are correct.
perChoice.c: The Standard SKU allows only Static assignment for both IPv4 and IPv6, so a Standard address cannot be created with Dynamic assignment; Dynamic assignment was only ever offered on the retired Basic SKU. A dynamic value is also not guaranteed to stay fixed, so the upstream allow-list would break whenever the value changes.
perChoice.d: The Basic SKU was retired on September 30, 2025, so it can no longer be used for new deployments and remaining Basic addresses must be moved to the Standard SKU. Basic addresses also do not support availability zones, so they cannot be deployed as zone-redundant in a region that has them, which breaks the requirement to survive a single zone loss.

body.stem: You have a public IP address pip-web-fe01 that is used by the front-end IP configuration of the public load balancer lb-web, which publishes a business web application from resource group rg-web-prod. Client browsers open long-lived HTTP sessions to the application, and the platform closes each session roughly four minutes after the last request arrives. Profiling the clients showed that a session can go completely quiet for up to twelve minutes and then continue normally. You need those sessions to survive such quiet periods. Which change should you make?

options.text: Set the idle timeout of pip-web-fe01 to 15 minutes.
Set the idle timeout of pip-web-fe01 to 45 minutes.
Set the idle timeout of pip-web-fe01 to 10 minutes.
Leave the idle timeout of pip-web-fe01 at 4 minutes.

explanation.correct: The idle timeout of a public IP address controls how long an inbound TCP/HTTP connection may remain idle before the platform closes it. The value is configurable between 4 and 30 minutes and starts at 4 minutes, which matches the roughly four-minute session drops reported. Because a client session can be silent for up to twelve minutes, the timeout must be at least twelve minutes; among the offered values, only 15 minutes both covers the measured quiet period and falls inside the supported range, so setting pip-web-fe01's idle timeout to 15 minutes is the right change.

perChoice.b: 45 minutes is beyond the maximum value of 30 minutes that can be configured for the idle timeout of a public IP address, so this change would not be accepted; the largest usable value is 30 minutes.
perChoice.c: 10 minutes sits inside the supported 4 to 30 minute range but is shorter than the twelve-minute quiet period the clients exhibit, so sessions that go silent for the full twelve minutes would still be closed by the platform.
perChoice.d: 4 minutes is the default and the value already in effect on pip-web-fe01, and it is precisely the interval after which sessions are being dropped today, so keeping it does not resolve the symptom.

body.stem:
You look after a long-lived public IP address that a partner's edge firewall has pinned to one host value, so the value of the address must not change while the business application keeps serving internet clients on TCP 443. Microsoft has retired the SKU this address was created with, and the addresses still sitting on that SKU have to be moved onto one that is still supported. The current configuration of the address and of the host it fronts is shown below.

Which change should you make?

options.text: Create a second Standard SKU public IP with a Static assignment, attach it to the IP configuration on nic-web-01, add an NSG rule that allows inbound TCP 443, and then delete the old Basic address.
Upgrade the existing pip-legacy-01 from Basic to the Standard SKU, keep its Static assignment and its current address value, and add an NSG rule on nic-web-01 that allows inbound TCP 443.
Upgrade the existing pip-legacy-01 from Basic to the Standard SKU and then change its assignment to Dynamic, so that the platform picks the address each time vm-web-01 starts.

Upgrade the existing pip-legacy-01 from Basic to the Standard SKU, keep its Static assignment and its current address value, and leave nic-web-01 without an NSG so inbound TCP 443 keeps flowing exactly as it does today.

explanation.correct: pip-legacy-01 still carries the Basic SKU, which Microsoft retired on September 30, 2025, so the address has to be moved to Standard through the documented upgrade path. Because the resource itself is upgraded rather than replaced and its assignment stays Static, the address value the partner pinned continues to be the one the application answers on. Standard public IP addresses are closed to inbound traffic by default, and nic-web-01 carries no network security group today, so an NSG with an explicit rule allowing inbound TCP 443 has to be part of the change or the application stops serving internet clients once the upgrade is done.

perChoice.a: Replacing the resource instead of upgrading it changes the address clients reach: a static address is assigned a value from the free pool in the location when the resource is created, and the value held by the old Basic resource is released when that resource is deleted and can never be recovered. The partner's allow-list for 203.0.113.24 would then point at an address the application no longer serves.
perChoice.c: Standard public IP addresses allow only a Static assignment for IPv4, so a Dynamic assignment is not available on this SKU. Changing the assignment from Static to Dynamic also means removing the address from the IP configuration and losing the current address value, which breaks the pinned allow-list requirement.
perChoice.d: Standard addresses are closed to inbound traffic by default, whereas Basic addresses were open by default. With no network security group on nic-web-01, the inbound TCP 443 flow is blocked after the upgrade, so the application is no longer reachable from the internet.

body.stem:
You have published the web application running on vm-web-01 in virtual network vnet-web (West US) behind a public front end, and clients reach it through the hostname webcontoso.westus.cloudapp.azure.com. IPv4 clients reach the application, but IPv6 clients get no response and the hostname publishes only an A record. The current configuration of the address and of the network interface it is attached to is shown below.

You need IPv6 clients to reach the same application through the same hostname. Which change should you make?

exhibit.text:
$ az network public-ip show --resource-group rg-web --name pip-web-fe-01
{
  "name": "pip-web-fe-01",
  "resourceGroup": "rg-web",
  "publicIPAddress": "20.62.8.31",
  "publicIPAddressVersion": "IPv4",
  "sku": { "name": "Standard" },
  "publicIPAllocationMethod": "Static",
  "dnsSettings": { "domainNameLabel": "webcontoso" },
  "ipConfiguration": {
    "name": "ipconfig1",
    "id": "/subscriptions/sub-001/resourceGroups/rg-web/providers/Microsoft.Network/networkInterfaces/nic-web-01/ipConfigurations/ipconfig1"
  }
}

$ az network nic ip-config list --resource-group rg-web --name nic-web-01
Name       PrivateIPAddress  PrivateIPAllocationMethod  PublicIPAddress
ipconfig1  20.62.0.4         Static                    pip-web-fe-01
ipconfig2  20.62.0.5         Dynamic                   null

options.text: Run the Azure CLI create command again for the public IP address resource pip-web-fe-01 with the IP version set to 'Both', then attach the result to the IPv6 IP configuration ipconfig2 on nic-web-01 using the same DNS name label.
Create a public IP address resource with an IPv6 address and Static allocation, then attach it to the IPv6 IP configuration ipconfig2 on nic-web-01 using the same DNS name label.
Enable IPv6 on the subnet of vnet-web and add an IPv6 private address to nic-web-01; the existing public IP address resource then publishes the AAAA record for the hostname.
Create an IPv6-only public IP address resource with Static allocation and attach it to the ipconfig1 IP configuration on nic-web-01 so that IPv6 clients reach the application.

explanation.correct: Serving IPv4 and IPv6 from one hostname on a NIC requires two address resources: one per address family. A single PowerShell or CLI create call only ever produces one address resource; the deployment that yields the two resources behind one name is the portal's 'Both' selection. Because the existing resource pip-web-fe-01 is IPv4 only and ipconfig2 has no public address, the missing piece is an IPv6 public IP address that is attached to the NIC's IPv6 IP configuration ipconfig2. On the Standard SKU only Static allocation is available for IPv6, so the new resource is created with a Static address, and the dual-stack pair can share one DNS name label, which makes the hostname publish both the A and the AAAA record.

perChoice.a: Every PowerShell or CLI create call creates a single address resource, so one command cannot produce the two resources a dual-stack pair needs; the 'Both' selection that deploys two resources is a portal capability. The name pip-web-fe-01 is also already taken in resource group rg-web, and names must be unique within the resource group, so this command would fail.
perChoice.c: Enabling IPv6 on the subnet and adding an IPv6 private address to the interface does not create a public IPv6 address, so nothing publishes an AAAA record for the hostname. The resource that is already deployed is IPv4 only and cannot add the IPv6 record.
perChoice.d: IPv6-only deployments are not supported: every network interface must keep at least one IPv4 configuration, so the IPv4 front end cannot be replaced by an IPv6-only one without breaking IPv4 clients. The resource also carries no DNS name label, so the hostname would gain no AAAA record.

body.stem:
You are writing the public front end section of a network design document for a platform that spans four components in East US 2. Each component in the table needs a public IP address, and the document must state the IP address assignment and the IP version that each component's front end can be given.

Drag each combination into the slot of the component it applies to.

rows: Provides outbound connectivity for the workloads in the virtual network vnet-core
Publishes the business web application running in the virtual network vnet-app
Terminates the private peering of the on-premises circuit in the virtual network vnet-hub
Public front end for the application servers in the virtual network vnet-portal

items.text: Static allocation, IPv4 only
Dynamic or Static allocation, IPv4 only
Dynamic or Static allocation, IPv4 or IPv6
Dynamic or Static allocation, IPv4 plus Dynamic IPv6 in preview

explanation.correct: Each component's front end accepts a specific set of allocation methods and IP versions, as listed in the Azure at-a-glance matrix of resource type versus public IP address assignment. A NAT gateway front end takes only a static IPv4 address, so it pairs with the static, IPv4-only combination. An Application Gateway front end is limited to IPv4, where the dynamic option belongs to the first version of the product and the static option to the second version. An ExpressRoute gateway front end takes dynamic or static IPv4 and can add dynamic IPv6, which is still a preview feature, while static IPv6 is not offered for it. A public load balancer front end accepts either allocation method and either IP version, including IPv6.

perChoice.i1: Belongs with the NAT gateway front end: that gateway accepts only a static IPv4 address and offers no IPv6.
perChoice.i2: Belongs with the Application Gateway front end: the address must be IPv4 because no IPv6 is offered, and the allocation method is dynamic on the first version of the gateway and static on the second version.
perChoice.i3: Belongs with the public load balancer front end: load balancer front ends accept both allocation methods and IPv6 as well as IPv4.
perChoice.i4: Belongs with the ExpressRoute gateway front end: that gateway accepts dynamic and static IPv4 and can also use dynamic IPv6, which is still a preview feature, whereas static IPv6 is not offered for it.

body.stem: You are building the public IP design for a platform deployed in East US 2. The list below shows six public endpoints, each with the single requirement raised by the team that owns it. Drag the value that the public IP address of each endpoint must be configured with into that endpoint's slot.

exhibit.text:
Public endpoint of the platform          | Requirement raised by the owning team
---------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Public address of vm-portal-01          | The address value is already written into a partner's edge firewall allow-list and that list cannot be edited, so the value the portal answers on must never change.
Front end of lb-report-01               | No DNS zone, certificate or partner system refers to the value, and the reporting service is stopped and started every month for patching.
Public address of af-prod-01             | The address has to be usable by a virtual machine, by a public load balancer and by Azure Firewall, and the platform team does not want to remain on the SKU that Microsoft has retired.
Front end of the load balancer that spans two continents | A single endpoint value has to be announced to clients in more than one location so that one hostname reaches both sides.
Front end of lb-intranet-01             | The endpoint serves only the workloads that sit in the same location, and no multi-location announcement is planned.
Public address of the outbound-heavy workload | Outbound traffic should leave the Microsoft backbone as early as possible so that the egress bill for the address comes down.

items.text: Static
Dynamic
Standard
Global
Regional
Internet

slots.label: Front end of the load balancer that spans two continents
Public address of the outbound-heavy workload

explanation.correct: Each endpoint's requirement maps to one setting of its public IP address. vm-portal-01 has a value pinned in a partner's allow-list, so the address must be Static, because a static value is allocated at creation and held until the resource is deleted. lb-report-01 has nothing depending on the value and is stopped and started monthly, so Dynamic fits, since a dynamic address may change after a deallocate and start. af-prod-01 must attach to a virtual machine, a public load balancer and Azure Firewall and must move off the retired SKU, so it needs the Standard SKU. The load balancer that spans two continents needs the Global tier, which provides anycast announcement from more than one location and is used with a cross-region Azure Load Balancer, while lb-intranet-01 serves a single location and takes the Regional tier. The outbound-heavy workload needs the Internet routing preference so that outbound traffic leaves the Microsoft backbone early and egress charges fall.

perChoice.a: Static belongs with the public address of vm-portal-01. A static address is allocated at creation and held until the public IP resource is deleted, so the value the partner's allow-list already contains keeps matching, and the value does not change while the portal runs.
perChoice.b: Dynamic belongs with the front end of lb-report-01. Nothing in the requirement depends on the value, and a dynamic address may change after the service is deallocated and started again, which the monthly patching routine tolerates.
perChoice.c: Standard belongs with the public address of af-prod-01. The Standard SKU supports attaching to virtual machines, public load balancers and Azure Firewall, and it replaces the Basic SKU that Microsoft retired on September 30, 2025.
perChoice.d: Global belongs with the front end of the load balancer that spans two continents. The Global tier provides anycast announcement across multiple locations and is used with a cross-region Azure Load Balancer.
perChoice.e: Regional belongs with the front end of lb-intranet-01. The Regional tier serves a single location, which matches an endpoint that announces only to the workloads in the same place.
perChoice.f: Internet belongs with the public address of the outbound-heavy workload. The Internet routing preference reduces the time outbound traffic spends on the Microsoft network and lowers egress charges; it requires the Standard SKU and cannot be changed after the address is created.

body.stem: You have five public IP addresses in East US 2 and need to record what happens to each address when the resources around it change. The table shows the current configuration of every address and the most recent change that affected it. Drag the outcome that belongs to each address into its slot.

rows: The association was removed from the IP configuration.
The virtual machine was deallocated and then powered on again.
The virtual machine was rebooted, and the operating system was also shut down from inside the guest.
The public IP address resource was deleted.
The address was detached from the NAT gateway, and the public IP address resource was kept.

items.text: The address is released and is no longer assigned to the resource.
The address may be given a different value afterwards.
The address keeps the value it already had.
The value is lost for good and cannot be recovered.
The address stays allocated to the public IP address resource until that resource is deleted.

explanation.correct: Each placement follows from the IP address assignment in the table combined with the change recorded for that address. A dynamically assigned address is released once its association is removed, can come back with a different value after a deallocate and start cycle, and keeps the same value through a reboot or a guest operating system shutdown. A statically assigned address stays with its own public IP address resource: detaching it leaves the value allocated to that resource, while deleting the resource discards the value permanently.

perChoice.i-rel: This belongs to pip-web-01, whose address uses dynamic assignment and was removed from the IP configuration. Removing the association releases a dynamically assigned address, so the address is no longer assigned to the NIC.
perChoice.i-chg: This belongs to pip-api-01, whose address uses dynamic assignment and whose virtual machine was deallocated and powered on again. A dynamically assigned address can change after a deallocate and start cycle, so a different value may be handed out afterwards.
perChoice.i-same: This belongs to pip-batch-01, whose address uses dynamic assignment and whose virtual machine was rebooted and shut down from inside the guest. Neither a reboot nor a guest operating system stop releases a dynamically assigned address, so the value stays as it was.
perChoice.i-lost: This belongs to pip-lb-fe01, whose address uses static assignment and whose public IP address resource was deleted. A statically assigned value is held only for the lifetime of its public IP address resource, so once that resource is gone the value cannot be recovered.
perChoice.i-held: This belongs to pip-nat-01, whose address uses static assignment and was detached from the NAT gateway while the public IP address resource was kept. Detaching a statically assigned address does not discard the value; it stays allocated to the public IP address resource until that resource is deleted.

body.stem: You are building the public front end of a new business application that will run behind a public Load Balancer named lb-app (Standard SKU) in resource group rg-app-prod in East US 2. The front-end IP configuration fe-app has no public address attached yet, so a new public IP address resource has to be created for it. The list shows the outcomes that the application, security and network teams have asked for, and the slots name the settings that the new public IP address resource exposes. Drag each outcome into the slot of the setting that delivers it.

exhibit.text:
PS C:\> Get-AzLoadBalancerFrontendIPConfig -LoadBalancerName lb-app -ResourceGroupName rg-app-prod

Name              : fe-app
PublicIPAddress   :
Subnet            :

items.text: Must keep answering clients even if one datacenter in the area fails
The IPv4 value must not change while the front end exists
Should spend as little time as possible on the Microsoft backbone to bring charges down
Must survive sessions that stay silent for a quarter of an hour
Must be reachable over IPv4 and over IPv6 through one hostname

explanation.correct: Each requested outcome is delivered by one specific setting on the public IP address resource, so every slot takes exactly one item. Surviving the loss of one datacenter comes from Availability zone set to Zone-redundant, because a zone-redundant address stays available through a single zone failure. A value that must never change comes from IP address assignment set to Static, since a static address is allocated when the resource is created and held until the public IP resource is deleted, which is what a pinned firewall allow-list requires. Reducing time on the Microsoft backbone and the egress charges that come with it comes from Routing preference set to Internet, which shortens the time traffic spends on Microsoft's network for supported resources; this setting cannot be changed after creation, so it has to be chosen now. Sessions that stay silent for twenty minutes need Idle timeout (minutes) set to 30, because that setting controls the inbound TCP or HTTP idle connection lifetime and can be set from 4 to 30 minutes, while the default of 4 would cut the session. Serving IPv4 and IPv6 clients through one name needs IP version set to Both, which deploys one IPv4 resource plus one IPv6 resource that share a single DNS name label publishing an A record and an AAAA record.

perChoice.o1: This outcome belongs with Availability zone. Choosing the Zone-redundant value keeps the address available through the failure of one zone, whereas Zonal ties the address to the health of a single zone and Non-zonal only fits locations that have no zones.
perChoice.o2: This outcome belongs with IP address assignment. Static allocates the address when the resource is created and holds it until the public IP resource is deleted, and it is the choice when firewall allow-lists or DNS records depend on a fixed value; Dynamic would let the value change after a deallocate and start.
perChoice.o3: This outcome belongs with Routing preference. Selecting Internet reduces the time traffic spends on Microsoft's network and lowers egress charges for supported resources, while Microsoft network is the default that keeps traffic on that network. The setting is locked once the resource exists, so it has to be picked at creation time.
perChoice.o4: This outcome belongs with Idle timeout (minutes). That setting defines how long an inbound TCP or HTTP connection may remain idle and accepts values from 4 to 30 minutes, so 30 covers a quiet period of twenty minutes while the default of 4 would end the session much earlier.
perChoice.o5: This outcome belongs with IP version. Selecting Both deploys two resources, one for IPv4 and one for IPv6, and the pair shares one DNS name label that publishes an A record for IPv4 and an AAAA record for IPv6, so clients of either family reach the front end through the same hostname.

body.stem: You are setting up the public addressing for a storefront platform in the West US region. The table lists the public endpoints involved and what the owning team asked for. Drag the outcome that belongs to each endpoint into that endpoint's slot.

rows: The IPv4 front end of the storefront. Clients reach it at the name that Azure registers for the address, and the label chosen is 'shopwest'.
The IPv6 address of the same storefront. It has to answer at exactly the name clients already use for pip-shop-fe01.
The front end of a Virtual Machine Scale Set whose members must be reachable from the internet.
The front end of a service that must answer on a name the company already owns.
A second copy of the IPv4 front end, wanted by another business unit in a different subscription, with the same label as pip-shop-fe01.

items.text: shopwest.westus.cloudapp.azure.com published as an A record
shopwest.westus.cloudapp.azure.com published as an AAAA record by the address created together with its IPv4 counterpart
A public IP prefix generates the addresses handed to the members, because the members have no public IP address objects of their own
The organization's own domain, answered through a matching record in the corporate DNS zone
Nothing is deployed, because the label is already taken in that region
Each member receives its own public IP address object, created in the resource group of the deployment

slots.label: Front end pip-shop-fe01 — IPv4 storefront address
Front end pip-shop-fe01v6 — IPv6 half of the same storefront
Front end pip-scale-fe01 — Virtual Machine Scale Set front end
Front end pip-custom-fe01 — service on a name the company already owns
Front end pip-shop-fe02 — duplicate in another subscription

explanation.correct: Each endpoint takes the outcome that follows from how Azure names and hands out public addresses. An IPv4 address with the label 'shopwest' in West US becomes shopwest.westus.cloudapp.azure.com, and Azure's default DNS publishes an A record for it. The IPv6 address of that storefront can only answer at the same name if it is created together with its IPv4 counterpart as one dual-stack pair, which is how a single name ends up carrying both A and AAAA records. A scale set's members have no public IP address objects of their own, so their addresses are generated by a public IP prefix. A name the company already owns is not served by the default zone, so a matching record must be created in the corporate DNS zone (or in Azure DNS). Finally, a label must be unique within the location across all subscriptions and all customers, so the duplicate requested for another subscription in the same region is blocked at deployment time.

perChoice.i1: Belongs to pip-shop-fe01: Azure appends the default suffix to the label, so 'shopwest' in West US becomes shopwest.westus.cloudapp.azure.com, and an IPv4 address is published with an A record.
perChoice.i2: Belongs to pip-shop-fe01v6: a dual-stack pair shares one name, so the IPv6 address created together with its IPv4 counterpart publishes the AAAA record for the name clients already use.
perChoice.i3: Belongs to pip-scale-fe01: there are no separate public IP objects for the instances of a Virtual Machine Scale Set, so a public IP prefix is what generates the instance addresses.
perChoice.i4: Belongs to pip-custom-fe01: a domain the organization owns is not covered by the default zone, so a matching record has to exist in Azure DNS or in an external DNS provider for clients to reach the address.
perChoice.i5: Belongs to pip-shop-fe02: the label is unique within the location across all subscriptions and all customers, so reusing 'shopwest' there fails and nothing is deployed.
perChoice.i6: Fits no slot: the members of a Virtual Machine Scale Set do not each get a public IP address object; their addresses come from a public IP prefix, which is the outcome already used for pip-scale-fe01.

body.stem: You have four public endpoints in a new platform deployed in West US. You need each endpoint to end up with the naming approach that satisfies the requirement in its slot. Drag the public IP address configuration that delivers each requirement into its slot.

items.text: Add a matching DNS record in Azure DNS or in an external DNS provider that points to the address.
Set a DNS name label so the label becomes a hostname under the Azure default domain with an IPv4 record.
Create an IPv4 and IPv6 address pair with a shared DNS name label and publish records for both address families.
Leave the DNS name label empty and reference the address directly.

slots.label: Corporate portal (vm-portal) — the organization owns fabrikam.com and wants visitors to reach the portal through that name.
Developer sandbox (vm-sbx) — the sandbox runs on IPv4 only, and the team wants an Azure-provided name that its IPv4 clients can resolve.
Partner ordering service (vm-partner) — clients on either kind of address must reach the service through the same name.
Industrial controller (vm-ctl) — the equipment reaches the service by numeric address only, and its environment cannot resolve names.

explanation.correct: The four slots call for four different naming outcomes. The corporate portal is published under fabrikam.com, a domain the organization already owns, so a matching record in Azure DNS or in an external DNS provider must point at pip-portal. The developer sandbox runs on IPv4 alone and needs the name that a DNS name label produces, published as an IPv4 record. The partner ordering service must be reached under one name from clients on either address version, which requires an IPv4 and IPv6 address pair that shares one DNS name label and publishes records for both families. The industrial controller has no name resolution in its environment, so its address keeps an empty DNS name label and is referenced by value.

perChoice.a: This belongs in the corporate portal slot: the portal is reached through the organization's own domain, so a matching record in Azure DNS or in an external DNS provider points clients at the address. A label would instead hand the portal an Azure-provided name.
perChoice.b: This belongs in the developer sandbox slot: the sandbox is IPv4-only, and a DNS name label yields the Azure-provided name with an IPv4 record. Publishing for two address families is not needed there.
perChoice.c: This belongs in the partner ordering service slot: only an IPv4 and IPv6 pair that shares one DNS name label publishes records for both address families under one name. The other endpoints do not need both families.
perChoice.d: This belongs in the industrial controller slot: the DNS name label is optional, and the controller's environment cannot resolve names, so the address is referenced by value with no label configured.

body.stem: You have a dual-stack storefront application running on virtual machine vm-shop-01 in East US 2, and the platform team deploys all public addressing with Azure CLI. The network interface nic-shop-01 has two IP configurations, ipconfig1 for IPv4 and ipconfig2 for IPv6, and only ipconfig1 carries a public address, so IPv6 clients cannot reach the storefront. You need IPv6 clients to reach the same application through the same DNS name label. Which action should you take?

exhibit.text:
az network public-ip create --resource-group rg-shop-prod --name pip-shop-04 --sku Standard --allocation-method Static --ip-version IPv4 --dns-name-label shopcontoso

$ az network public-ip list --resource-group rg-shop-prod --output table
Name          ResourceGroup   ProvisioningState   IPVersion   PublicIPAddress
----------    --------------  ------------------  ---------   --------------
pip-shop-04   rg-shop-prod    Succeeded           IPv4        20.62.18.41

$ az network nic ip-config list --resource-group rg-shop-prod --nic-name nic-shop-01 --output table
Name       PrivateIPAddress   PublicIPAddress
---------  -----------------  ------------------
ipconfig1  10.20.1.4         20.62.18.41
ipconfig2  2001:db8:8a2e::9  <none>

body.statement: The correct action for the team is {{action}}.

options.text: Run the create command again with the IPv6 version and a new name, then attach it to the NIC's IPv6 IP configuration.
Run the create command again with the IPv6 version and the same name, then attach it to the NIC's IPv6 IP configuration.
Run the create command once with the Both version and attach the result to both IP configurations.
Create a Public IP Prefix with the IPv6 version and attach it to the NIC's IPv6 IP configuration.

explanation.correct: Each PowerShell or Azure CLI command creates a single public IP address resource, so the team needs a second command with the IPv6 version to produce the second address for the dual-stack NIC. That second resource also needs its own name, because public IP address names must be unique within the resource group, and it should use the Standard SKU, which permits only Static allocation for IPv4 and IPv6. Assigning the second address the same DNS name label makes the hostname publish both an A record for the IPv4 address and an AAAA record for the IPv6 address, and attaching the resource to ipconfig2 lets IPv6 clients reach the storefront.

perChoice.action:b: Public IP address names must be unique within a resource group, so the second IPv6 resource cannot reuse pip-shop-04. When you create an IPv4 and an IPv6 address, you specify a different name for each resource.
perChoice.action:c: The portal's Both selection deploys two resources, but each PowerShell or Azure CLI command creates only one address resource, so a single command with the Both version doesn't yield the second address, and one resource can't be attached to both IP configurations.
perChoice.action:d: A Public IP Prefix generates the instance addresses for a Virtual Machine Scale Set; it isn't attached to a network interface's IP configuration, so it can't supply this NIC with an IPv6 address.

body.stem:
You have a public IP address pip-api-01 in resource group rg-api of subscription sub-api-001, deployed in East US 2 with the IP address assignment set to Static. It is the public front end of the IP configuration ipconfig1 on network interface nic-api-01, which serves virtual machine vm-api-01. The application team wants the address to stop holding one fixed value for that machine, so it can take a different value each time the virtual machine is deallocated and started, and they want this done on the existing pip-api-01 resource because the operations tooling and the corporate access policy both refer to that resource by name. The current configuration of the address is shown below.

Which change should you make?
body.statement: The change that satisfies the team's requirement is {{slot1}}.

options.text: Change the IP address assignment of pip-api-01 from Static to Dynamic while ipconfig1 keeps using it, and expect the current address value to be kept.
Remove pip-api-01 from ipconfig1, change the IP address assignment from Static to Dynamic, then associate pip-api-01 with ipconfig1.
Change the IP address assignment of pip-api-01 from Static to Dynamic in place, and delete the Azure DNS A record that maps the name label to the old value.
Delete pip-api-01, create a new public IP address with the IP address assignment set to Dynamic instead of Static and the same name label, and point ipconfig1 at the new address.

explanation.correct: A public IP address can only be switched from a fixed (Static) allocation to a Dynamic allocation when it is first taken out of the IP configuration that it serves. The right sequence is therefore to remove pip-api-01 from ipconfig1, change the IP address assignment to Dynamic, and then associate pip-api-01 with ipconfig1 again, which is what keeps the existing resource (and the references other teams hold to it by name) in place. The original address value is lost by this change, and the address can take a different value on a later deallocate and start of the virtual machine, which is exactly what the application team wants.

perChoice.slot1:a: This option tries to change the IP address assignment while ipconfig1 is still using the address, but the assignment can only be changed after the public IP has been removed from the IP configuration. It also wrongly implies that the current address value survives the change: the original address is lost when the assignment moves to Dynamic.
perChoice.slot1:c: The in-place change has the same flaw as the other in-place variant, because the address must first leave ipconfig1. Deleting the Azure DNS A record is not what enables the address to change either: Azure DNS keeps its mapping for the name label, and the address value itself changes only after the resource is moved to a Dynamic assignment.
perChoice.slot1:d: Deleting pip-api-01 is unnecessary and destructive: a deleted public IP address cannot be recovered, and the team explicitly needs the existing resource, which the tooling and access policy identify by name, to keep serving ipconfig1. The assignment change is achieved by taking the address out of ipconfig1 and putting it back, not by building a replacement resource.

body.stem: You have a public IP address pip-sql-01 with the DNS name label sqlgw in resource group rg-sql-prod in East US 2. It is attached to IP configuration ipconfig1 of network interface nic-sql-01, which belongs to virtual machine vm-sql-01. The corporate edge firewall allow-lists the current address value, and the public DNS entry for the service points at pip-sql-01. You need to retire vm-sql-01 and replace it with vm-sql-02 and its new network interface nic-sql-02 in the same resource group, while the service keeps running on the same address value and the DNS entry stays exactly as it is. Which sequence of actions should you use?

rows: Created separately from the virtual machine by the platform team
vm-sql-02 (replacement, created without a public address)

options.text: detach pip-sql-01 from nic-sql-01, delete vm-sql-01, then attach pip-sql-01 to nic-sql-02
detach pip-sql-01 from nic-sql-01, set the assignment to Dynamic, delete vm-sql-01, then attach pip-sql-01 to nic-sql-02
delete pip-sql-01 and vm-sql-01, then create a new Static public IP address and attach it to nic-sql-02
move pip-sql-01 to resource group rg-sql-02, delete vm-sql-01, then attach pip-sql-01 to nic-sql-02

explanation.correct: A public IP address is its own resource, and the address stays dedicated to whatever it is attached to only until you detach it or that attached resource is deleted. Removing pip-sql-01 from nic-sql-01 before retiring vm-sql-01 keeps the public IP resource and its Static value alive; the same resource can then be attached to the new interface, so the allow-listed address value and the existing DNS name label are both preserved.

perChoice.sequence:b: Switching an address from Static to Dynamic discards the original value, and a Dynamic value can change again after a deallocate and start, so the allow-listed address and the DNS mapping would no longer be dependable. That change also requires removing the address from the IP configuration first.
perChoice.sequence:c: Deleting pip-sql-01 releases its address permanently and the value cannot be recovered. A newly created Static address is chosen by Azure from the free pool in the location, so the allow-listed address value would be lost even though the new address is also Static.
perChoice.sequence:d: Moving the resource to a different resource group does not protect the address. Deleting vm-sql-01 removes nic-sql-01, and the address is released when the resource holding it is deleted, so the value cannot be carried over to nic-sql-02 in this order.

body.stem:
You support the hub virtual network vnet-hub in West Europe for a hybrid estate. On-premises users reach the estate through the VPN gateway vpngw-hub, which is connected to vnet-hub. The network team plans to add an IPv6 address range to vnet-hub so that new workloads can be addressed with IPv6, and the plan introduces a group of virtual machines that will run in the new IPv6 subnet with an IPv6 configuration only. The current configuration of the estate is shown below.

Which statement belongs in the deployment plan?
body.statement: The deployment plan records that {{slot1}}, and that {{slot2}}.

options.text: the VPN gateway stops serving the virtual network
the VPN gateway keeps serving the virtual network in the same way as today
the VPN gateway starts serving IPv6 traffic for the virtual network
the VPN gateway starts serving IPv6 traffic for the virtual network once it is given a public IP address created with the Both version setting
each machine requires dual-stack configuration
each machine can be given IPv6-only configuration
each machine can be given IPv6-only configuration when a public IP address is created with the Both version setting
each machine can be given IPv6-only configuration because IPv6-only virtual machines are supported

explanation.correct: Two separate constraints decide the wording of the plan. First, a VPN gateway cannot serve a virtual network that has IPv6 enabled, whether the network is connected directly or reached over a peer connection; once the IPv6 address range is added to vnet-hub, vpngw-hub falls outside its supported scope, so the plan must record that the gateway stops serving that network (or the range must not be added while the gateway serves it). Second, IPv6-only virtual machines and scale sets are not supported: every network interface needs at least one IPv4 configuration, so any IPv6 deployment has to be dual-stack. The planned machines therefore cannot carry an IPv6 configuration alone, and the plan must state that each of them requires dual-stack configuration.

perChoice.slot1:b: A VPN gateway cannot serve a virtual network that has IPv6 enabled, so it does not continue serving vnet-hub unchanged once the new address range is added.
perChoice.slot1:c: A VPN gateway has no IPv6 capability; it cannot pick up the new address range and begin forwarding IPv6 traffic for the virtual network.
perChoice.slot1:d: The Both version setting applies to the public IP address resource and creates one IPv4 resource plus one IPv6 resource for that address. It does not give a VPN gateway any IPv6 capability.
perChoice.slot2:b: IPv6-only virtual machines and scale sets are not supported. Every network interface needs at least one IPv4 configuration, so a machine planned with an IPv6 configuration alone cannot be deployed.
perChoice.slot2:c: Creating a public IP address with the Both version setting produces an IPv4 resource plus an IPv6 resource for that address, but it does not replace the IPv4 configuration that every network interface still needs.
perChoice.slot2:d: The premise is wrong: IPv6-only virtual machines and scale sets are not supported in Azure, and every network interface needs at least one IPv4 configuration.

body.stem: Your company publishes one application from two Azure regions, East US 2 and West Europe, and clients on both continents must reach the service through the same address. The cross-region Azure Load Balancer that fronts it is already deployed and the company has signed off on using it, but its front-end IP configuration fe-global-01 has no public address attached yet, so a public IP address resource still has to be created for it. A partner firewall allows inbound TCP 443 only to the address value, so that value must stay the same for as long as the service runs, and the partner's monitoring probes only speak IPv4. Which public IP address resource should you create for fe-global-01?

exhibit.text:
Deployment facts for the front end
-----------------------------------------
Load balancer             : lb-global-app (Standard SKU), cross-region
Front-end IP configuration: fe-global-01, no public address attached yet
Regions served            : East US 2 (primary), West Europe (secondary)
Partner firewall          : inbound TCP 443 allowed to the address value only; value must not change
Partner monitoring        : IPv4 probes only

body.statement: You should create the front end's public address with {{pipConfig}}.

options.text: Standard SKU, Global tier, IPv4, Static assignment
Standard v2 SKU, Global tier, IPv4, Static assignment
Standard SKU, Regional tier, IPv4, Static assignment
Standard SKU, Global tier, IPv4, Dynamic assignment

explanation.correct: The public front end of a cross-region Azure Load Balancer is served by an address whose tier is the multi-region anycast one, and that tier is offered only by the Standard SKU; it isn't yet offered by the Standard v2 SKU, whose addresses can be used only with the Standard v2 NAT gateway. A Standard address allows only static allocation for IPv4, so the value is reserved at creation and never changes while the resource exists, which is what the partner's allow-list needs, and the IPv4 version matches the partner's IPv4-only probes.

perChoice.pipConfig:b: Standard v2 addresses don't yet support the multi-region tier, and they can be used only with the Standard v2 NAT gateway, so a v2 address can't be the public front end of a cross-region load balancer.
perChoice.pipConfig:c: A Regional tier address belongs to a single region. Only the multi-region tier address is used with the cross-region Azure Load Balancer, so a regional address can't front it.
perChoice.pipConfig:d: Standard addresses support only static allocation. A dynamic address isn't assigned when the resource is created and can change after the attached resource is deallocated and started, which would break the partner's allow-list.

body.stem: You operate the customer portal on a Virtual Machine Scale Set named vmss-portal with 60 instances in East US 2, and the instances are published straight to the internet on TCP 443. The corporate edge firewall allow-lists the address that each instance presents, so that address has to keep the same value for as long as the instance lives. The platform team wants one single resource to supply the addresses for all of the instances, and company policy forbids creating new public addressing on a SKU that Microsoft has retired. Which resource and settings should you create for the scale set?

exhibit.text:
Workload          : Virtual Machine Scale Set vmss-portal (60 instances)
Location          : East US 2
Published service : TCP 443, reached directly from the internet
Edge firewall     : The address presented by each instance is allow-listed and must not change while that instance exists
Address source    : One single resource should supply the addresses for all of the instances
Company policy    : No new public addressing may use a SKU that Microsoft has retired

body.statement: Create a {{resource}} with the {{sku}} SKU and an IP address assignment of {{assignment}}, and attach it to the scale set so that each instance receives one of the addresses it holds.

options.text: Public IP Prefix
Public IP Address
NAT Gateway
Application Gateway
Standard
Basic
Standard v2
Static
Dynamic

explanation.correct: Instances of a Virtual Machine Scale Set do not carry individual public IP address objects; a Public IP Prefix is the resource that generates the addresses handed to those instances, so it is the single resource that satisfies the platform team's requirement for one shared source of addresses. The edge firewall allow-lists the value each instance presents, and a Dynamic address is only allocated once the resource is associated and running, is released when the association is removed and can change after a deallocate and start, so the IP address assignment must be Static to keep the allow-list valid. On the SKU, Basic was retired on September 30, 2025 and company policy forbids new public addressing on a retired SKU, while a Standard v2 address can be attached only to a Standard v2 NAT Gateway and never to another product or component, so the Standard SKU is the correct choice for scale set addressing.

perChoice.assignment:a2: A Dynamic address arrives only after the resource is associated and the workload is started, is released when the association is removed, and can change after a deallocate and start. That would break the allow-list entry that pins each instance's address.
perChoice.resource:r2: A Public IP Address is attached to a single IP configuration, such as the one on a virtual machine network interface or a load balancer front end. Scale set instances do not receive their own public IP address objects, so creating one of these per instance is not how the instances get their addresses.
perChoice.resource:r3: A NAT Gateway provides outbound connectivity for outbound-originated flows from the subnet and does not publish inbound traffic to the instances, so it cannot front the scale set for the internet-bound TCP 443 service.
perChoice.resource:r4: An Application Gateway is a reverse-proxy front end that carries its own front-end address; it is not the resource that generates the addresses the scale set instances use.
perChoice.sku:s2: The Basic SKU was retired on September 30, 2025, and company policy forbids creating new public addressing on a retired SKU. Basic also cannot be mixed with Standard in the same scale set design.
perChoice.sku:s3: A Standard v2 address attaches only to a Standard v2 NAT Gateway and never to another product or component, so it cannot supply the addresses of the scale set instances.
